answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, randomly select players + 1 face-down for the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The player with the lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; play then proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: “randomly select number of players + 1”; “one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: At setup, put each character on its home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining that base; four mechs over the abilities on the Faction Mat; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in the Player Mat bottom-row circular spaces; the remaining six workers on the Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat, ready for its first placement. Leave the Faction Mat one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. The Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw. Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards)”; starting-piece table lists the placements.

answers.answer: You may take either action, both, or neither, but must move the token to a different section. If taking both, take the top before the bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Before an action, pay its full exposed red-box cost; exposed green-box benefits are optional and may be taken partly or not at all. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades. Never pay only part of a cost; if unable to afford any action, move the token and take neither.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “either, both, or neither, but must move the token”; “bottom first is not allowed”; “First pay the full cost”; “You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost.”

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay action costs with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control/resources: “An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources”; “Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even to act elsewhere.”

answers.answer: No. A normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A mech may carry any number of your workers, but not your character; characters, mechs and workers can each carry any number of resources. Being carried does not count as the worker's own movement, so the carried worker may subsequently move itself. A worker can also move onto a mech and be carried by its later move.
answers.evidence: Move: “two different units, one adjacent territory each”; “Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers”; “Being carried does not count as the worker's own movement.”

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech stops and cannot move again that turn when it enters a territory with enemy workers only. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base and leave resources behind; the player loses one popularity per worker, down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers; Speed applies to character/mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Move: “Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops”; workers “immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources”; “Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero”; “Speed adds one territory ... not workers.”

answers.answer: After all units finish moving in the Move action, resolve combats between opposing characters/mechs sharing a territory, before any following bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Combat: “After all units finish a Move action ... fight, before any subsequent bottom action. The attacker chooses the order”; movement rules prohibit workers moving independently “into or out of” enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card (before upgrades). If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard pile are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity (before upgrades). Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
answers.evidence: Bolster: “Pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card”; empty-deck rule. Trade: “Pay $1”; resources go “on a controlled territory containing at least one worker”; cannot Trade for resources if all workers are home.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full before production; the costs can be power, popularity and/or coins. Then choose up to two different controlled territories. Each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right after payment and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers newly exposed on the mat affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: “Pay every exposed Produce cost ... in full before production”; “Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right, after payment”; “Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid”; “You may decline some or all production.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs oil: move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box on the Player Mat; this improves a top benefit and reduces a bottom cost. Solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: place a chosen mech from the Faction Mat on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Upgrade — oil”; “Deploy — metal”; mech placement and ability effects; “Even after completing all ... you may still pay for that bottom action.”

answers.answer: Build by paying wood and place a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker. Only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents' structures; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives an extra Produce territory and produces as one worker, but only while you control its territory; it can produce without an actual worker there. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, and can be used even when enemy units occupy its territory. Opponents cannot use your building abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: “controlled territory with your worker”; “Structures cannot be moved or destroyed”; Mill bonus applies “only while controlled”; Mine is a personal tunnel “even when enemy-controlled.”

answers.answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, regardless of the one-time choice: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. When triggered by a bottom-row action, resolve active player first, then immediate left neighbor, then immediate right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent gets the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit from “any bottom-row section” to “any open one-time recruit bonus”; four one-time bonuses; ongoing bonus is “the circle uncovered where you removed the recruit.” Ongoing recruits specify active → left → right and two-player opponent triggers once.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly sets dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even at zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if any workers are present. If both players have combat mech abilities, the attacker uses theirs first, then the defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Each player loses the dial power they committed from their power track, and all played cards are discarded face-up; card values do not cost additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: dial from “0 to the smaller of seven and your current power”; “one combat card per participating character/mech”; abilities “attacker uses theirs first, then defender”; attacker wins ties; dial payment and card discard.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (ordinary limit of two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within the six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers onto adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4: winner controls territory/resources and star eligibility; losing units retreat “leaving all resources”; step 5: attacker popularity loss and loser combat-card draw condition.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on its token territory; then discard the token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter option's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs apply and no mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses, are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there”; if entry is lost “the token stays”; gains go to “the encounter territory”; “Pay no additional normal action costs and gain no additional mat benefits.”

answers.answer: Every player's character must take a Factory card on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if needed. The player chooses one available card and returns the rest; this applies to each player, not only the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Similar Factory actions do not grant the corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory card's bottom action moves one unit up to two territories during that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; normal movement/stop restrictions and Mine access apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: “Every player's character” takes a card on its “first finish of a Move action”; one permanent card, no later exchange; fifth action section; bottom action moves one unit up to two or three with Speed; no corresponding mat bonuses.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives: “Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action”; meet “all requirements at the moment of reveal”; put “both objective cards on the bottom”; Saxony can score both.

answers.answer: A star is earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent once placed even if power or popularity later drops. Other players' stars never block a goal. The game ends immediately when someone places their sixth star.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all nine achievements; says “Other players' stars never block a goal,” a placed star “is permanent,” and the sixth star “immediately ends play.”

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins and the player's ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, resolve the active player first, then the left neighbor, then the right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at every step; if an earlier player ends the game, later recruit stars or bonuses do not resolve. If units are still intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning the initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth star: collect “primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star”; recruit sequence active → left → right; pending battle movement is undone and no further combat resolved.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is $4, each controlled territory is $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources is $2. Five stars yield $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory count as seven territories total and yield $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and yield $12. These add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus. You earn the selected structure bonus even if enemies control your structures' territories. The winner is the player with the most total coins; ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Scoring table at popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per resource pair. Factory “counts as three territories total”; example gives $20 + $21 + $12 = $53. Structure bonus applies “even if enemies control your structures' territories”; tie-break list follows.
